title: That Angel - Who Is She?
paragraphs: The confidant, though mischievous, is virtuous by disposition. His affection for the hero is boundless much like the waves of the sea getting gravitated towards the shore.

At dusk, the friend saw the hero surging ahead. He called him by clapping, “Why such an undue haste as if you were heading for a feast? I am back after seeing an angel under the waning moonlight. She is none but a goddess; I witnessed the scene of her stepping out of the temple and standing near the entrance.”
After hearing this from his friend, The hero resolved to see her. He literally flew towards the direction pointed at by the friend, like a kite pouncing upon a parrot.
Without even an atom of doubt, she is a goddess! Decked in the ornaments, She appeared before him. Finding her as an embodiment of beauty, He surged quite close towards her, in measured steps.

Since a goddess does not speak, There was no opportunity for him to speak out and clear his doubt. He dared to analyze her through eyes and see whether she is a goddess. Since a bee kept relishing the flowers
From her hair flowing down And as only the flowers sported by the humans Emit fragrance, It dawned upon him that she was no goddess.
He looked at the ornaments on the body And saw that they were all the ones made by the goldsmith of this world.

Having finished his study on half of her body, He was in raptures understanding that she was not a goddess. The drawings on her breasts and shoulders seen, And the fragrance of lily flower held by her smelt, And known for certain That the eyes on her rounded moon-like face Were but the human eyes all flesh and blood, Also clearing his mind that If she were an angel, her eyelids would not twitch like this And seeing that she was perturbed after noticing him, a man, It was all obvious that She was not an angel but a pigeon Who came searching for him.
The fact of her being a human fully dawned on him. And the prankster pal was embarrassed and hid himself near the bush Realizing the emerging scene of his friend and the lady united.

> The swarming bees, the ornaments worn, > The ornamental lines drawn on the body, > The fading flowers, human eye, signs of disquietude > The winking of eyes and timidity > And such of these that mark the person > There manifest for the doubt to vanish. > > (Poruḷatikāram : Kaḷaviyal, verse 4)
